tests.precondition: Brand source publishes 12 brands, including one wide (landscape) and one tall (portrait) source logo. A zero-brand fixture is also available.

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu and locate the carousel.
steps.result: A carousel strip renders below all product category columns, spanning the full panel width.

steps.action: Record the panel height, then reload with the zero-brand fixture and record it again.
steps.result: The panel height is identical in both cases — the carousel does not alter it.

steps.action: With 12 brands, count the logos fully visible without scrolling.
steps.result: Between 5 and 7 logo items are visible simultaneously.

steps.action: Resize to the narrow end of the desktop range and reopen the megamenu.
steps.result: The carousel still renders and the visible count adapts to the panel width, with no partially clipped logo at the strip edge.

steps.action: Inspect every logo container, including the wide and tall source logos.
steps.result: Each container is circular at a 1:1 aspect ratio; each logo is centred, undistorted, and does not overflow the circle.

tests.summary: [EC-18] Arrow controls — scrolling, boundaries and disabled states
tests.precondition: Products megamenu open at 1440x900 with 12 brands authored. Track at its leftmost position.

steps.action: Inspect the carousel for arrow controls.
steps.result: Both a previous-brands and a next-brands arrow button are rendered and visible.

steps.action: Inspect the previous-brands arrow at the start of the track.
steps.result: It carries aria-disabled="true", is styled as disabled, and remains in the tab order.

steps.action: Focus the previous-brands arrow and press Enter, then Space.
steps.result: The track does not move; its scroll offset is unchanged.

steps.action: Activate the next-brands arrow once.
steps.result: The track advances by one item width and a later set of brands becomes visible.

steps.action: Activate the previous-brands arrow once.
steps.result: The track rewinds by exactly the same amount, restoring the original set.

steps.action: Scroll fully to the end of the track and inspect the next-brands arrow.
steps.result: It carries aria-disabled="true", remains in the tab order, and activating it produces no movement.

steps.action: Scroll from start to end and back, observing both arrows throughout.
steps.result: Both arrows remain present and visible at every scroll position; neither is removed from the DOM nor hidden.

steps.action: Leave the megamenu open and untouched for 60 seconds.
steps.result: The track does not move at any point — no auto-play or auto-scroll occurs.

tests.precondition: Products megamenu open at 1440x900 with 12 brands authored. Keyboard input only.

steps.action: Tab into the carousel region.
steps.result: Focus enters the carousel and the focused element shows a visible focus indicator.

steps.action: Press ArrowRight.
steps.result: The track advances by the same increment as an arrow-button activation.

steps.action: Press ArrowLeft.
steps.result: The track rewinds by the same increment.

steps.action: Press Tab repeatedly through the brand links.
steps.result: Focus advances to each brand link in turn; pressing Tab does not itself scroll the track.

steps.action: Press Escape.
steps.result: Focus leaves the carousel and returns to the megamenu panel, consistent with the megamenu's defined Escape behaviour.

tests.precondition: Mobile drawer open on the Products section at 390x844 with 12 brands authored.

steps.action: Locate the brand logos in the Products drawer section.
steps.result: A horizontal strip of circular brand logos renders inline in the drawer.

steps.action: Inspect the entire drawer markup for arrow controls.
steps.result: No previous or next arrow button exists anywhere below 1024px.

steps.action: Swipe the strip horizontally with a quick flick.
steps.result: The strip scrolls smoothly and continues briefly with momentum.

steps.action: Drag the strip slowly with a pointer and release.
steps.result: The strip follows the drag and settles without snapping back unexpectedly.

steps.action: Swipe vertically starting from inside the strip.
steps.result: The drawer scrolls vertically as normal; the gesture is not swallowed by the strip.

tests.summary: [EC-18] Variant switching and shared data source
tests.precondition: Brand source publishes 12 brands and can be edited and re-published. Repository checkout of the branch under test is available.

steps.action: At 1440x900, inspect the desktop megamenu panel markup.
steps.result: Only the arrow-controlled desktop variant is present; no mobile-strip variant renders in the panel overlay.

steps.action: Resize the window below the breakpoint and reopen the navigation.
steps.result: The mobile strip variant renders and no arrow buttons are present.

steps.action: Resize back above the breakpoint and reopen the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The arrow-controlled desktop variant renders again.

steps.action: Add one brand to the authored data source, publish, then reload on desktop.
steps.result: The new brand appears in the desktop carousel.

steps.action: Reload on mobile and open the Products drawer.
steps.result: The same new brand appears in the mobile strip, sourced from the same authored data.

steps.action: Inspect the repository for the carousel implementation.
steps.result: Exactly one implementation exists, named brands-carousel; there are no separate desktop-only and mobile-only implementations.

tests.precondition: 12 brands authored, each with a valid destination URL.

steps.action: On desktop, open the Products megamenu and click the first brand logo.
steps.result: The browser navigates to that brand's authored destination URL and the destination page renders.

steps.action: Return to the test page and open the Products drawer on mobile.
steps.result: The brand strip is visible in the drawer.

steps.action: Tap the first brand logo.
steps.result: The navigation drawer closes and the browser navigates to the authored destination URL.

steps.action: Inspect the destination page.
steps.result: No drawer or overlay remains on screen.

tests.precondition: Two fixtures available: the brand source returning zero rows, and the brand source request failing (blocked or HTTP 500).

steps.action: With the zero-row fixture, open the Products megamenu and inspect the panel markup.
steps.result: No carousel container, strip, heading or arrow button exists in the DOM — not merely hidden with CSS.

steps.action: Inspect the panel layout.
steps.result: Category columns fill the panel with no empty gap where the carousel would sit.

steps.action: Inspect the browser console.
steps.result: No uncaught error is logged.

steps.action: Switch to the failing-request fixture and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The carousel zone is absent from the DOM and the megamenu remains fully usable.

steps.action: Inspect the browser console.
steps.result: A warning is logged for the failed fetch and no uncaught exception is thrown.

tests.summary: [EC-18] Authored content variations and slot fallbacks
tests.precondition: 12 brands authored. One brand has a logo URL pointing at a non-existent file, one has no destination URL, and one has no brand name. Fixtures exist both with and without a section heading.

steps.action: With a section heading authored, locate it relative to the strip.
steps.result: The authored heading text renders directly above the carousel strip.

steps.action: Switch to the fixture with no heading authored and inspect the markup.
steps.result: No heading element is present in the DOM — not an empty or whitespace-only one.

steps.action: Locate the brand whose logo URL is broken.
steps.result: Its circular container renders with a placeholder background showing the brand initials or accessible label.

steps.action: Activate that brand.
steps.result: The link is still active and navigates to its authored destination.

steps.action: Inspect the brand that has no destination URL, then attempt to activate it by click and by keyboard.
steps.result: It renders without an anchor and produces no empty or broken href; activating it navigates nowhere and throws no error.

steps.action: Inspect the brand that has no name authored in the accessibility tree.
steps.result: Its image is exposed as decorative with empty alt text, and its link still has a non-empty accessible name derived from the filename or a generic fallback.

tests.precondition: Brand data source response throttled to roughly 3 seconds.

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu and observe the carousel zone during the delay.
steps.result: Placeholder space matching the final carousel height is reserved.

steps.action: Inspect the carousel region while it is still loading.
steps.result: The region carries aria-busy="true" and a visually hidden status message such as "Loading brands" is present.

steps.action: Press Tab repeatedly while loading is still in progress.
steps.result: No brand link receives focus while the loading state is active.

steps.action: Wait for the data to arrive and inspect the region again.
steps.result: aria-busy is removed, the brand links become focusable, and surrounding content does not move as the logos appear.

steps.action: Record Cumulative Layout Shift attributable to the megamenu during load.
steps.result: No layout shift is attributed to the carousel zone.

tests.precondition: Page rendered with dir="rtl". Products megamenu open at 1440x900 with 12 brands authored.

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu and observe the resting position of the track.
steps.result: The first authored brand appears at the right-hand edge and the track scrolls right-to-left.

steps.action: Activate the arrow that advances the list.
steps.result: The track advances toward the end of the authored order, mirrored correctly.

steps.action: Activate the arrow that goes back.
steps.result: The track rewinds correctly in the mirrored direction.

steps.action: Inspect the accessible name of each arrow button.
steps.result: Names describe logical direction (next / previous brands), are not swapped, and are not described by visual position.

steps.action: With focus inside the carousel, press ArrowRight and then ArrowLeft.
steps.result: Keyboard scroll direction matches the mirrored layout consistently with the arrow buttons.

tests.notes: RTL coverage is a standing requirement for every block, applied here in addition to AC-8.

tests.summary: [EC-18] Accessibility semantics and screen reader output
tests.precondition: Products megamenu open at 1440x900 with 12 brands authored. A screen reader is available.

steps.action: Inspect the accessibility tree for the carousel.
steps.result: The carousel is exposed as a region with a meaningful accessible name, via aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing at the section heading.

steps.action: Inspect the accessible name of every brand link.
steps.result: Each equals its authored brand name; none is empty, generic, or a filename.

steps.action: Inspect the arrow controls in the accessibility tree.
steps.result: Both are exposed as buttons with descriptive accessible names.

steps.action: Navigate through the carousel with a screen reader.
steps.result: The region boundary is announced and each brand is announced as a link with its brand name.

tests.precondition: 12 brands authored, section heading authored. Desktop fixture at 1440x900 and mobile fixture at 390x844. Track at its leftmost position so one arrow is disabled.

steps.action: Focus each interactive element in turn and measure the focus indicator contrast against its background.
steps.result: A focus indicator is visible on every arrow and logo link, each at a contrast ratio of at least 3:1.

steps.action: Measure the contrast of the enabled arrow icons and the heading text against their backgrounds.
steps.result: All meet the WCAG 2.1 AA minimum for their size and role.

steps.action: View the disabled arrow in greyscale.
steps.result: Its disabled state remains discernible without colour, through opacity, icon treatment or another non-colour cue.

steps.action: Inspect the disabled arrow's accessible state.
steps.result: aria-disabled="true" conveys the state programmatically.

steps.action: Measure the rendered hit area of each brand logo link on mobile.
steps.result: Every touch target is at least 44px by 44px.

steps.action: Run an automated accessibility scan (axe or equivalent) against the open megamenu.
steps.result: No WCAG 2.1 AA violations are reported for the carousel region.

tests.notes: AC-26 (European Accessibility Act / ADA) is a legal framework rather than a checkable behaviour. Conformance is evidenced by the WCAG 2.1 AA checks in this test. A separate audit artifact, if required, is a compliance sign-off rather than a test case. WCAG AA coverage is a standing requirement for every block.

tests.precondition: Fixtures available with 1 brand, 3 brands (fewer than the visible slots) and 20 brands.

steps.action: With the single-brand fixture, open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The carousel renders with the one brand in a correctly formed circular container; the layout is not stretched or broken.

steps.action: Inspect the arrow controls with one brand.
steps.result: No scroll action is offered, since there is nothing to scroll to.

steps.action: Switch to the 3-brand fixture and inspect the carousel.
steps.result: No scrollable overflow exists; the arrows are either absent or permanently disabled and offer no scroll action.

steps.action: Switch to the 20-brand fixture and scroll from start to end.
steps.result: All 20 brands are reachable, the layout does not break, and no partially clipped logo is left at rest.
